actor: Media-ingest provenance detection engineer, Meta Platforms
job: Standing up manifest extraction on every image and video entering Instagram, Facebook and Threads, not only items Meta's own generator produced.
outcome: A corpus-wide provenance check already run against uploaded content, so answering for one item costs a lookup rather than a fresh scan.
motivation: The platform cannot know at ingest which of an item's future viewers will be Californian, so the check has to cover everything.

task.who: Meta media infrastructure and content integrity engineering teams
task.what: Extract provenance manifests at ingest across all uploads
task.where: Meta's media upload and asset processing pipeline
task.why: A Californian's question cannot wait for a later scan
task.how: Manifest validation libraries wired into upload worker jobs

actor: Content Credentials verification SDK maintainer, Adobe Content Authenticity Initiative
job: Hardening the open-source provenance validation libraries platforms embed, so manifest checks survive platform-scale throughput and truncated or adversarial inputs.
outcome: A verification library a covered platform can run across its whole corpus without writing its own parser for a signed manifest.
motivation: Platform adoption stalls at the point where a platform would have to build and maintain signature validation itself.

task.who: Adobe and Content Authenticity Initiative open-source library maintainers
task.what: Harden the open-source provenance verification library for platform scale
task.where: The Content Credentials open-source repositories and tooling releases
task.why: Platforms will not hand-roll a signed manifest parser
task.how: Rust and JavaScript libraries shipped with conformance test vectors

actor: Video transcoding and delivery engineer, Google's YouTube platform
job: Keeping signed provenance manifests attached through the re-encoding, thumbnailing and delivery steps that today discard almost all embedded media metadata.
outcome: Delivered media still carrying its provenance data, so the platform can offer inspection or download with the data attached.
motivation: The statute forbids knowingly stripping provenance, which turns an encoder that silently drops manifests into a compliance defect.

task.who: YouTube media processing, transcoding and content delivery engineers
task.what: Preserve signed provenance manifests through transcode and delivery
task.where: YouTube's encoding ladder and content delivery pipeline
task.why: Stripping provenance in the encoder is itself a violation
task.how: Manifest-preserving encoder profiles plus regression tests on output assets

job: Scoping what the second California tranche obliges Snapchat to detect and display, and whether the display control can be geofenced.
outcome: A written compliance scope treating detection as corpus-wide and placing the user-facing control on one code path rather than two.
motivation: Five thousand dollars a violation a day, with three classes of plaintiff, makes an ambiguous second code path the expensive option.

task.who: Snap legal, privacy and regulatory compliance counsel
task.what: Scope the covered-platform provenance duty for Snapchat
task.where: Snap's regulatory compliance review and product legal sign-off
task.why: Daily-accruing penalties reward the least ambiguous compliance surface
task.how: Line-by-line statutory mapping against Snapchat's distribution surfaces

actor: Consumer protection enforcement attorney, California Department of Justice
job: Preparing enforcement of the AI Transparency Act's platform tranche, including which provenance specifications count as widely adopted and standards-body adopted.
outcome: A stated enforcement position naming qualifying provenance specifications, closing the reading under which a platform detects nothing and displays nothing.
motivation: A statute naming neither the specification nor the body leaves covered platforms a defence the Attorney General has to foreclose.

task.who: California Attorney General's consumer protection and technology enforcement staff
task.what: Publish an enforcement position on qualifying provenance specifications
task.where: California Department of Justice guidance and enforcement planning
task.why: An unnamed specification is the platforms' cheapest way out
task.how: Statutory interpretation reviewed against adopted standards-body publications

actor: Specification and conformance program lead, Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
job: Moving the content provenance specification through a recognised standards body and running the conformance program that says which implementations count.
outcome: A provenance specification a platform's counsel can cite as widely adopted and adopted by an established standards-setting body.
motivation: Until the specification has standards-body standing, a covered platform can argue nothing qualifies and ship no control at all.

task.who: C2PA specification editors and conformance program administrators
task.what: Advance the provenance specification through a recognised standards body
task.where: C2PA working groups and the conformance program registry
task.why: The statute defers to a body it declines to name
task.how: Standards-body submission plus a published implementation conformance registry

actor: Consumer product manager for content transparency, TikTok
job: Designing the per-item surface reporting whether provenance data is attached to a video and naming the generative system or capture device found.
outcome: A provenance detail control on an ordinary item, reachable by an ordinary account the platform does not place in California.
motivation: Once detection runs corpus-wide, hiding the control behind a geolocation check buys a second code path and a story nobody wants.

task.who: TikTok content transparency product management and design teams
task.what: Ship a per-item provenance detail control in-product
task.where: TikTok's in-app item detail and content-info surfaces
task.why: A policy page cannot satisfy a user-interface obligation
task.how: Item-level interface reading the already-computed provenance index

actor: Transparency enforcement officer, European Commission AI Office
job: Enforcing Article 50's machine-readable marking duty and running the transparency Code of Practice its signatories use to demonstrate compliance.
outcome: Marked synthetic media across the single market, giving a platform's detection layer the same substrate a California provenance control reads.
motivation: A marking obligation with no marked content behind it produces detection that finds nothing and a control nobody bothers to ship.

task.who: AI Office transparency unit and national market surveillance authorities
task.what: Enforce machine-readable marking of AI-generated media
task.where: EU market surveillance casework and the transparency code process
task.why: Detection needs marked content before it finds anything
task.how: The voluntary transparency Code of Practice and its signatory list

actor: Camera firmware engineer for in-camera provenance signing, Sony
job: Shipping firmware that signs capture metadata in the camera body, ahead of the capture-device tranche the same California statute dates to 2028.
outcome: Camera-signed images circulating on covered platforms, so a provenance control has capture devices to name and not only generative systems.
motivation: A control that only ever reports generative systems answers half the statute, and camera signing is the half manufacturers own.

task.who: Sony imaging firmware and digital signature engineering teams
task.what: Extend in-camera provenance signing across shipping camera bodies
task.where: Sony Alpha firmware releases and signing key infrastructure
task.why: Platforms can only name a capture device that signed
task.how: Hardware-backed signing keys writing provenance claims at capture
